properties.otherAdvice:
Roads around Circular Quay and The Rocks, and in Milsons Point will close during the day and evening for Australia Day events in the city and around the harbour.

Key road closure timings:

  • 4am to midnight: George St from Essex St to Hickson Rd, and sections of OPT Elevated Rd from Hickson Rd, Circular Quay West, Essex St and Pitt St.
  • 7am to 10am: Hickson Rd from Napoleon St to Pottinger St, Towns Pl from Dalgety Rd to Hickson Rd and Barton St (for Oz Day 10K wheelchair race).
  • 7am to midnight: Hickson Rd from George St to Pottinger St.
  • 6:30pm to 10:30pm: Sections of Macquarie St.
  • 7:30pm to 10:30pm: Cahill Expressway lanes 7 & 8 and Overpass at Circular Quay including the High St, Mount St and Domain Tunnel on-ramps and lane 4 on the Harbour Bridge. Roads in Circular Quay north of Bridge St including sections of Albert St, Alfred St, Circular Quay East, Conservatorium Rd, Dalley St, Essex St, George St, Loftus St, Pitt St, Philip St, Macquarie St, Reiby Place, Underwood St and Young St. 
  • From 9:15pm to 10:15pm: Sections of Argyle St, Grosvenor St, Bridge St and Harrington St.
  • The speed limit on the Harbour Bridge will be reduced to 40km/h from 7:30pm to 10.30pm.
  • The Cahill Expressway Circular Quay overpass walkway will be closed from 5pm to 9:30pm. The Sydney Harbour Bridge Walkway and Cycleway will remain open.
  • Milsons Point/Kirribilli 10:30am to 1pm: Olympic Drive between Broughton St and Alfred St South.
  • 7.30pm to 10.30pm: Lane 4 on the Harbour Bridge, Cahill Expressway lanes 7 and 8 and the Circular Quay Overpass will close. High St and Mount St on-ramps from North Sydney and Kirribilli will also be closed.

Special event clearways will be in effect on various roads in Circular Quay and The Rocks from 3am until midnight and throughout the CBD from 5pm until 10.30pm.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types, and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

Thousands of participants are expected to take part in the annual Sun Run event. The 7km run starts at 6:30am and the 10km run starts at 7.15am, both from The Strand in Dee Why with both events finishing at Manly Beach by 10am.

Road closures, parking restrictions and changed traffic conditions will be in effect starting at 3:30am. All roads will reopen by 11am. 

Residents along the course are urged to plan ahead and relocate their vehicles outside the road closure footprint if vehicle access is required on event day. There will be limited vehicle movements permitted while the event is underway. 

ROAD CLOSURES

  • Dee Why – from 3:30am to 9am: sections of Howard Ave, The Strand and Dee Why Pde, The Oaks Ave westbound crossover will be maintained at The Strand until 6am.
  • Dee Why – from 5:15am to 9am: sections of Oaks Ave, The Stand, Boronia St, Griffin Rd and Monash Pde will be closed.
  • Dee Why – from 6am to 9am: sections of Pacific Pde will be closed.
  • North Curl Curl to Freshwater – from 5:30am to 9am: sections of Abbott Rd, Griffin Rd, Pitt Rd, Adams St, Carrington Pde, Charles St, Evans St and surrounding local roads will be closed. Crossover points will be maintained on Pacific Pde at Griffin Rd, Playfair Rd at Pitt Rd, Ross St at Pitt Rd and Headland Rd at Griffin Rd until 6:15am.
  • North Curl Curl – from 6am to 9am: Headland Rd will be closed eastbound between Wheeler Pde and Griffin Rd.

Special event clearway parking restrictions will be in effect from 3am until 9am on roads along the course through Dee Why, North Curl Curl, Freshwater, Queenscliff and Manly, including on sections of Abbott Rd, Howard Ave, The Strand, Evans St, Crown Rd North Steyne and South Steyne.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

NBL: Sydney Kings v Melbourne United at Qudos Bank Arena. Tip-off at 7.30pm, full time around 9.30pm.

Traffic will be heavier than usual on roads approaching Sydney Olympic Park as attendees travel to the match in the busy evening peak.

Motorists should allow extra travel time on roads including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry.

Sydney Olympic Park Authority may close local roads in the precinct to ensure pedestrian safety during events. View the interactive map for closure details.

Luke Combs – Live in Australia 2025 at Accor Stadium in Sydney Olympic Park on Friday 31 January and Saturday 1 February. Support act from 6pm, Luke Combs on stage from 8.45pm and finish around 10.45pm each concert night.

With more than 160,000 fans epected over both concert nights, significant traffic delays are expected on roads approaching the precinct and entering car parks, particularly during Friday’s evening peak travel times.  

Motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time on roads approaching Olympic Park including on the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

  • CAR PARKS: parking in the precinct is in high demand and expected to sell out before the event. Ticketholders who have to drive must pre-book parking ahead of time to secure a space.
  • If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry.
  • Alternatively, consider parking at a nearby train station commuter car park and continuing your trip by train to Olympic Park, at no extra cost.

Sydney Olympic Park Authority will close local roads in the precinct to ensure pedestrian safety during events and accommodate additional transport services. For road closure details, view the interactive map.
